page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.large is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on KVM virtualization. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical CPU core with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache setup includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration flags.

The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio typical of memory-intensive cloud architectures. It does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for operating system and data volumes. Networking performance is specified with a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core processing capabilities, placing in the top tiers for stress-ng and Geekbench single-threaded tests. However, total multi-core compute and overall PassMark CPU scores reflect lower tier results due to the limited total allocation of two vCPUs across a single physical core. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth hover in average bands at 45.05 GB/sec and 26.33 GB/sec, while static web throughput and Redis operations settle in lower brackets.

Given its high memory allocation per core, Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.large delivers cost efficiency for workloads constrained by memory footprint rather than heavy parallel computation. It is appropriate for lightweight caching tiers, small in-memory databases, development environments, and memory-dependent microservices that demand high per-thread execution speed over aggregate multi-core scaling.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core, complemented by 16.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage, relying entirely on network storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps with no attached GPUs. Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-threaded compute performance alongside average uncached memory bandwidth, though overall multi-threaded capacity remains constrained by the 2-vCPU count. The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable resource efficiency for workloads that require significant memory headroom without extensive parallel processing demands. It is well-suited for lightweight in-memory databases, intermediate caching layers, microservices, and general memory-oriented enterprise workloads.
